items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: And I’m sure Oscar Peterson has had some bad reviews, but I can’t say that he’s suffered from jazz criticism.

ctx.x: Oh sure. Nobody likes to be told that their hands are dirty. That’s what criticism means. You mother is saying, “Go wash your hands again before you come to dinner.” That’s why we call it the jazz journalists instead of critics. There is really very little serious criticism that’s done in the name of publication work anyway these days. I think that like any profession the jazz journalists are still learning how to do what they do, and they’re not all at the top of their metier. I think that there’s no training in…

certainly in jazz journalism or music criticism. So a lot of us just kind of stumble around trying to figure out how to do it and how to do it right and how to do it well. So I think that the musicians have a point when they say well this guy doesn’t know what he’s talking about. Not all of us do know what we’re talking about. That’s not to criticize my colleagues, that’s to give them credit for trying to talk about something which as I said before is quite elusive, quite ethereal and insubstantial. And how to…
